import pandas as pd

# List of source file paths as given
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/training_9.csv"
]

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# According to operation_history, UNION all these source tables
# All source tables have the same schema ['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']
# So we can concatenate them directly

target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure the target schema and types:
# 'admit': integer, 'gre': integer, 'gpa': float, 'prestige': integer

target_df = target_df.astype({
    'admit': 'int64',
    'gre': 'int64',
    'gpa': 'float64',
    'prestige': 'int64'
})

# Write the result to the specified path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_87/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
